answerToTheDispatch.rootCauseOfTheZoningZeros: FOUR stacked causes, not one. The dispatch's framing (written, served, scored zero) is correct in every part, and the first mechanism that fits it is wrong.

causes.label: VERIFIED
causes.name: A silent table fallback manufacturing a positive absence
causes.detail: locateCounty() prefers txgio_parcel and falls back to txgio_parcel_staging, which has NO zoning_district column. On the fallback hasZoning=false, sourcePresentForStampFacet returns false, and classifyFacet emits `true-source-gap` - defined in the file's own header as 'the facet has no data because the SOURCE has none, an honest absence' - at 0.00% with a NULL source. That is an absence written from the instrument's blindness. 15 zoning rows in production carry exactly that shape.
causes.evidence: information_schema.columns: txgio_parcel has zoning_district, txgio_parcel_staging does not. Live rows: 15 zoning rows with source NULL, classification true-source-gap, honest_coverage_pct 0.00.

causes.label: VERIFIED
causes.name: A denominator the rail cannot pass, and a classification that hides it
causes.detail: Coverage is stamped / ALL county parcels against a 95% depth threshold, while 23 city zoning layers are wired (ZONING_LAYERS) against 1,222 incorporated-city boundaries in tx_city_boundary. 244 of 254 counties can only ever produce 0.00% - and the scorer classified that as `real-at-ceiling`, which asserts the achievable ceiling IS zero. Reproduced live on Dallas 48113 (30-plus incorporated zoned cities, none wired): 0.0% -> real-at-ceiling. So the two false-absence classifications point in opposite directions and between them cover every unmeasurable county.
causes.evidence: Object.values(ZONING_LAYERS).length = 23 across 10 counties; SELECT count(*) FROM tx_city_boundary = 1222; county_rail zoning thresholdPct 95.00 coverageClass jurisdiction-depth.

causes.label: VERIFIED
causes.name: The single satisfied zoning cell is not a zoning measurement
causes.detail: Bastrop 48021's zoning row is byte-identical to its ENVELOPE row: both 99.77%, both source 'deterministic', both source_vintage 'layer-23-city-mu', both classification 'true-source-gap', both checked_at 2026-08-03T15:16:48.373Z. classifyFacet can NEVER emit true-source-gap with non-zero coverage, so neither row came from the checked-in classifier. Bastrop's measured zoning stamp rate is 9,642 of 63,357 = 15.22% county-wide, and 100.00% within its stamped jurisdiction. The vintage string 'layer-23-city-mu' matches no artifact in the repo (grep returns nothing) and Bastrop's ArcGIS zoning layer is /83, not /23, so the row's author is UNIDENTIFIED. What is established is what it is NOT: not the county-wide stamp rate, not the in-jurisdiction rate, and not a product of this repo's classifier.
causes.consequence: The reading that 'zoning depth is ONE county' rests entirely on this cell.

answerToTheDispatch.whatTheFirstPlausibleMechanismWouldHaveB: That the scorer measures a different substrate from the atoms - SCORED reading txgio_parcel while WRITTEN/SERVED ride the atom store. The atom chain is baked FROM the column the scorer reads. Recorded because the dispatch asked for the cause and not a cause.

facetKeyFixAndOrphanDisposition.theDefect: countyCoverageScoreCli.ts wrote facet 'land-use'; the rail key is 'landuse'; manifestGridRead joins c.facet = r.rail_key. 19 rows written, joined by nothing, read by no cell.
facetKeyFixAndOrphanDisposition.verdict: NEITHER a rename NOR a read-time alias. Both assume the two keys measure the same thing. Measured, they do not.
facetKeyFixAndOrphanDisposition.proof: All 19 counties already hold a 'landuse' row from a DIFFERENT measurement: source 'land-use-fact-atom-count' (atom coverage, written 2026-08-12 by score_cad_rails_fast.mjs) versus 'cad-roll' / 'cad-roll-address-join' (roster-to-CAD JOIN RATE). The rail row is newer in all 19 and HIGHER in all 13 currently satisfied-present (48027 77.76 vs 98.90, 48091 0.00 vs 99.68, 48113 92.83 vs 99.91, 48491 89.14 vs 99.85). The primary key is (county_fips, facet), so a rename is an OVERWRITE that would drop counties out of satisfied-present. A read-time alias is worse: the grid join is 1:1 and two candidate rows for one cell have no tie-break rule.
facetKeyFixAndOrphanDisposition.theFix: The CAD-roll join rate now writes under the DECLARED NON-RAIL key 'landuse-cad-join'. lib/db/src/schema/facetKeyRegistry.ts makes the legal key set data derived from COUNTY_RAIL_DECLARATION, assertWritableFacetKeys fails closed before any write, and the divergence test rejects NEAR MISSES (land_use, Landuse, foot-print) that no set-equality control could see. Join quality was ruled not-a-rail on 2026-08-08, and the declaration carries that ruling.
facetKeyFixAndOrphanDisposition.whatHappensToTheExistingRows: They stay put in this PR. countyFacetKeyReconcileCli.ts re-keys them to 'landuse-cad-join', dry-run by default, --apply refused while any primary-key conflict stands, rolling back rather than leaving a partial re-key, and printing the counter-evidence against a merge on every run. Dry-run verified against production 2026-08-19: 19 rows, 0 conflicts. The apply was NOT run - a production write and a retirement are operator rulings (DEV_PROCESS 5.4).

verdictOnThe19VersusOne.theTwoNumbers: 19 = rows in county_facet_coverage with facet='zoning' and rail_state='satisfied-present'. 1 = zoning cells the live ledger displays as satisfied-present. Both VERIFIED by this lane.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.verdict: The gate is CORRECT in its refusal and DEFECTIVE in what it erases. It is not a third defect in the sense of being wrong to fire.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.whyTheRefusalIsLoadBearing: countyCoverageScoreCli.ts — the scorer that owns zoning, envelope and land-use — did not write county_facet_coverage.rail_state, while its two sibling scorers do (countyFloodScoreCli.ts line 210, countyGeometryScoreCli.ts line 445). So for exactly those facets the coverage number and the field the display reads had different authors and no consistency constraint, which is how Travis came to hold rail_state='satisfied-present' at honest_coverage_pct=0.00 with verified_by_instrument NULL. Until that is applied, applyDepthRailDisplayGate is the only thing standing between such a row and a customer-facing 'satisfied'.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.whatIsActuallyDefective: The gate sets isPartial=false while demoting, so 'measured at 33.98% below a 95% bar' renders identically to 'never scored at all'. VERIFIED live: ALL 18 partial cells in the entire ledger are zoning cells - a jurisdiction-depth rail - so the summary field built to surface that class, satisfiedPresentPartialCells, reads 0 on the deployed endpoint while the store holds 18. A purpose-built indicator that cannot fire for the only class populating it is the DEV_PROCESS 2.2 shape.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.whyItWasNotFixedHere: Making it fire requires changing what the summary counts, which moves a reported number. Filed for the operator. The current behaviour is PINNED by a divergence test across BOTH implementations so the ruling cannot land in one of them.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.alsoFound: applyDepthRailDisplayGate exists TWICE - lib/db/src/manifestGridRead.ts and artifacts/api-server/src/countyLedgerCompute.ts - with two hand-maintained copies of the manifest-grid SQL feeding them. One rule, two implementations, nothing comparing them: the CTRL-1 shape. The gate functions are now covered by a real divergence test; the duplicated SQL is not, and that residual exposure is stated in the test's own header.
verdictOnThe19VersusOne.nowFixed: This lane implemented the sibling pattern: deriveRailState writes satisfied-present at or above the declared threshold and not-yet below it, carrying the real coverage; satisfied-absent is unreachable from a stamp-rate scorer by design; the non-rail diagnostic facet writes a NULL rail_state. It takes effect only when the operator runs the scorer with --apply.

operatorRulingsRequested.ruling: Applying the fixed scorer takes Texas from 1 satisfied zoning cell to 0.

The fixed scorer measures Bastrop zoning at 15.22%. This is a CORRECTION, not a regression, but it moves a launch-gate number.
operatorRulingsRequested.recommendation: Accept the correction. A launch gate that closes because the number was never a zoning measurement is the failure the manifest exists to prevent.

operatorRulingsRequested.ruling: Whether the zoning denominator becomes incorporated-city parcels rather than all county parcels.

NOTE the trap: the tempting shortcut - stamped / parcels-with-a-zoning_jurisdiction - is a TAUTOLOGY that returns 100.00% for every wired county, because the same PIP writes both columns. Measured on six counties: all 100.00%.
operatorRulingsRequested.recommendation: Yes, but as its own lane with the PIP built properly. Until then the county-wide rate stays, with its counting rule now written into the row.
